Every install gets a name.

The network name and its own certificate, the wifi door, following a peer by name.

source docs/ai/team-sync-by-network-name.md · last changed c42370683 2026-10-29

Status (2026-10-14): design only, no product code. Builds on docs/ai/one-local-address.md (§5 guest path, §9 owed) and di-atlas decisions/every-install-gets-a-name.md (2026-09-12). Every claim is marked VERIFIED (read in code or a cited page, 2026-10-14) or PROPOSAL. Words follow docs/ai/vocabulary.md: an install is one machine's di, a space is yours inside it, a place is the real room.

1. What the owner asked (2026-10-13)

"when we work with the team and everyone installs and works together, it needs to be synced … I installed di and I have diiii.localhost, my version … diiii. … Ponyo installs the same … and if needed she can send the same with ip and there will be synced." His two decisions: 1. Any machine can be the hub. People follow each other's di by a network name; no dev server in the room. 2. Private until the wifi door opens, then instant. The name and certificate are prepared while private; opening the door only opens the door.

Unchanged: your own address is http://diiii.localhost/ on every machine (VERIFIED, PR #893: di status leads with it; the certificate's name is one line phones and headsets: …, scripts/di/ui.mjs phonesLine).

2. What exists today

  • local.thedi.studio is one hand-made record plus one certificate, on aylmo only (VERIFIED, atlas decision; the domain is on Cloudflare, the API token stays with the owner). Nobody else has a name.
  • di up --lan binds 0.0.0.0 per start and calls the owner's ~/.di/dns-update hook (VERIFIED, scripts/di/cli.mjs ~L164–214, scripts/di/name.mjs updateRoomName). Going public needs a restart.
  • --lan without --guests "hands every visitor the owner's whole estate" (VERIFIED, comment in cli.mjs).
  • di invite <space> mints a per-space, editor-scoped, revocable sync key; di follow <space> --from <url> --key … [--at <address>] follows it; --at is the address pin: name kept for Host/SNI/certificate, socket sent to the given address (VERIFIED, scripts/di/share.mjs pinnedLookup, cli.mjs cmdFollow).
  • The place address and its QR panel: GET /serverXR/api/guest-address reads the name out of the served certificate; states ready/not-on-network/no-certificate/wildcard (VERIFIED, serverXR/src/guestAddress.js, src/landing/GuestAddressPanel.jsx). A wildcard certificate gives no address today (VERIFIED).
  • The door on :80 serves one exact name and answers 421 to any other Host — the DNS-rebinding guard (VERIFIED, serverXR/src/localName.js). The rig beacon is UDP broadcast, HMAC-signed with a rig secret (VERIFIED, serverXR/src/rig/discovery.js). avahi-publish gives di.local (VERIFIED, name.mjs).
  • There is no di wifi command (VERIFIED, cli.mjs command table).

3. Research (read 2026-10-14)

Topic Finding Source
Plex Each server gets its own wildcard *.<hash>.plex.direct (DigiCert); the IP is encoded in the label (192-168-1-5.<hash>.plex.direct) and DNS decodes it. Separate domain from plex.tv. Valsorda, "How Plex is doing HTTPS for all its users" (2015)
sslip.io / nip.io Stateless DNS: 192-168-0-1.sslip.io answers 192.168.0.1; open-source Go server; a subdomain can be delegated to it. sslip.io, wildcard.md
Tailscale tailscale cert gets Let's Encrypt certs for *.ts.net names; Tailscale writes the DNS-01 TXT, the private key is made and kept on the machine; names land in public CT logs. Tailscale KB 1153 "Enabling HTTPS"
Let's Encrypt DNS-01 Proves control by a TXT record; no open port; the only way to get a wildcard. LE challenge types
LE limits 50 new certificates per registered domain per 7 days, shared by every account; 5 per exact name set per 7 days; 5 auth failures per name per hour. "300 new orders per account per 3 h" is unverified (page text not reachable from here). LE rate limits
Cloudflare Workers free: 100,000 requests/day, 10 ms CPU; paid from $5/month. API: 1,200 requests per 5 min per user. Workers pricing, API limits
Rebind protection OpenWrt dnsmasq drops public answers that point at private addresses unless the domain is in rebind_domain; dnsmasq 2.93 (OpenWrt 25.12.5) also counts 100.64/10, which broke *.ts.net until listed. FRITZ!Box: "Domain name exceptions", cannot be turned off. OpenWrt DHCP/DNS, OpenWrt forum 251494, AVM KB 663
mDNS .local is not a potentially trustworthy origin, so plain http there has no camera/mic/WebXR; no public CA issues .local; name conflicts rename hosts. W3C Secure Contexts §3.1, RFC 6762 §9

4. The name (PROPOSAL; claim and certificate BUILT 2026-10-28, PR 2)

  • Label: <who>-<4 chars>, e.g. ponyo-k7q2, dob-a3f9. <who> comes from the di login account; the 4 chars are random and make it unguessable-enough and unique per machine (one person, two laptops, two names).
  • Network name: ponyo-k7q2.<zone>; <zone> is l.diiii.xyz or a separate domain (Q1).
  • Certificate: one per install, names ponyo-k7q2.<zone> and *.ponyo-k7q2.<zone>. The wildcard also covers the address-in-name form 192-168-15-53.ponyo-k7q2.<zone> (atlas decision) if §5 B is ever turned on.
  • BUILT (PR 2, branch feat/di-name-2026-10-28, tested against a fake broker and a fake ACME client only): di name / --status / --renew / --forget in scripts/di/networkName.mjs + nameStore.mjs; files in ~/.di/name/; di status prints the name line; di up and di autoupdate run renew at < 30 days, at most once a day (the CLI exits after di up, so the timer's tick is the daily check). Zone l.diiii.xyz; ACME through acme-client 5.4.0 pinned in serverXR/package.json (what a packed install runs npm ci for). Not yet run against the real broker or Let's Encrypt. scripts/di/name.mjs is the older mDNS (di.local) file, unrelated.
  • What a person types: the label only — di follow show --from ponyo-k7q2. The CLI adds the zone.
  • The address stays http://diiii.localhost/ for yourself; the network name is for other machines.

5. How it resolves

A. Per-install record through a broker (recommended first, PROPOSAL). The broker writes one A record per install in the Cloudflare zone, TTL 60. While private it points at 127.0.0.1 (a record that exists avoids a cached "no such name" delaying the door); when the door opens it moves to the LAN address. Uses only Cloudflare's DNS; no new server. Cost: one API write per door opening and per address change.

B. Stateless address-in-name (later, Q3, PROPOSAL). Delegate <zone> (NS) to an sslip.io-style server on the VPS; 192-168-15-53.ponyo-k7q2.<zone> answers itself, nothing is ever written, opening the door needs no DNS write at all. Cost: running authoritative DNS (port 53, two servers for redundancy). The QR would use this form.

C. No DNS at all, between installs on one wifi (PROPOSAL, §8). The beacon says "ponyo-k7q2 is at 192.168.15.53:443"; the follower pins it (--at, VERIFIED mechanism). Works with the internet cut.

6. Each install gets ITS OWN certificate, never our Cloudflare token (PROPOSAL)

The name broker is a Cloudflare Worker holding a token limited to DNS edit on <zone> (Cloudflare tokens scope to a zone, not a subdomain — a reason for Q1). Flow, Tailscale-style: 1. Claim (once, after di login): the install makes an Ed25519 install key, sends its public half plus its di login token. The broker checks the account with the dev tier once, stores label → {account, pubkey} in KV. 2. Certificate: the install runs its own ACME client (its own LE account key), makes its TLS key locally, and for each DNS-01 challenge asks the broker, signed with the install key, to set _acme-challenge.ponyo-k7q2.<zone> TXT; the broker deletes it after. The TLS key never leaves the machine. 3. Address: signed PUT address moves the A record — accepted only for loopback, RFC 1918, 100.64/10 and IPv6 ULA, so our domain can never front a public host (no phishing by name). 4. Abuse limits: 3 labels per account; 4 orders per label per week; 60 address writes per label per hour; writes only under the caller's own label; bad signatures counted and blocked; the owner can revoke a label (record + KV) in one call; a removed account loses its labels. Files: the install's name certificate lives in ~/.di/name/ — not ~/.di/tls/, so aylmo's local.thedi.studio certificate is never touched (VERIFIED: ~/.di/tls/ is what di up serves today, paths.mjs).

7. THE WIFI DOOR — one command, one button, instant (BUILT 2026-10-28, PR 3: serverXR/src/wifiDoor.js, routes/wifiDoorRoutes.js, scripts/di/wifiCmd.mjs, src/landing/WifiPanel.jsx; not yet run on a real phone or a real certificate)

Prepared ahead, while private (at di login or the first di up after it): claim the label, get the certificate, record at 127.0.0.1. Nothing listens on the wifi. di status says the name is ready. WIFI (di wifi, or the Wifi button on the local home top bar; the existing Phones & headsets door /#join becomes the Wifi panel): 1. the server opens a wifi door: a listener on the LAN address, port 443 (else the install's port), added at runtime like the :80 door — no restart (today --lan needs one); 2. the door serves only the install's own names (421 otherwise, the localName.js rule) and always as --guests: a visitor is a guest with a sandbox and the open space, never the owner's estate; 3. the broker moves the record to the LAN address (or nothing, under §5 B); the beacon starts announcing; 4. the panel shows the QR of https://ponyo-k7q2.<zone>/ and the line for di people: di follow <space> --from ponyo-k7q2 (+ --key, from di invite, which stays per space). Close door (di wifi --stop, same button): door closed, record back to 127.0.0.1, beacon silent. After a restart the install is private again, like --lan today; the Wifi button is pressed again (the name and certificate are kept). A restart closes the door but the broker keeps the last address it was given (measured 2026-10-29: 06:11 restart, the name still answered the wifi address). So a start points the record home: one signed PUT 127.0.0.1 about 5 s after start (one retry after 60 s), logged as name record pointed home. di wifi --stop on an already closed door does the same now; di wifi --status says when the name still points at a wifi address while the door is closed. The name certificate's CN is the plain name, so guest-address reads one address from it (VERIFIED rule: CN first).

8. di follow --from <name>, peer to peer (BUILT 2026-10-28, branch feat/follow-by-name-2026-10-28; two-machine offline proof still owed)

di follow show --from ponyo-k7q2 --key dii_sync_… resolves the address in this order, and keeps the name for Host, SNI and the certificate check every time (the address pin, VERIFIED): 1. the beacon on this wifi: a new unsigned di-name announcement {label, port}; an announcement is only a hint — trust comes from the certificate, which a liar cannot present; 2. DNS of the network name (§5 A/B); 3. the last address that worked (stored with the follow). Offline on one wifi: step 1 is enough; certificate checks need no internet. Owed measurement from one-local-address.md §9.6: two machines, internet cut. Any machine can be the hub: the follow engine already carries ops and files both ways (VERIFIED, CURRENT.md "Follow"); a chain dob → ponyo → kiara works because each install is both. Across the internet: out of scope — the dev tier, or Tailscale with --at (VERIFIED, exists).

9. What di status prints (PROPOSAL)

http://diiii.localhost/  — di.iiii running                         (unchanged first line, #893)
private · name ready: ponyo-k7q2 (certificate until 2027-01-12) · di wifi to open it

Open:

http://diiii.localhost/  — di.iiii running
open on this wifi (192.168.15.53) · phones and headsets: https://ponyo-k7q2.l.diiii.xyz/
following: show ← dob-a3f9 (this wifi) · 2 follow you

One line when something is wrong, naming the fix: name not ready: broker unreachable — retry at next di up, the router hides ponyo-k7q2 from phones — see di wifi --router.

10. Address changes and renewals (PROPOSAL)

  • DHCP: while open the server checks its addresses every 10 s; on change the door rebinds, the broker moves the record (TTL 60), the beacon says the new address. Followers find it by beacon within seconds.
  • Several interfaces (wifi + cable + Tailscale): the default-route interface; di wifi --on <address> picks.
  • Renewal: LE certificates last 90 days; renew at 30 days left, at di up and daily while running. A failed renewal never touches http://diiii.localhost/; di status says the date. LE has announced shorter lifetimes (unverified schedule) — the daily check covers that.
  • LE limit: 50 per registered domain per week (VERIFIED) is shared by every install and the owner's other diiii.xyz certificates. 90-day renewals mean about 400 installs before it binds — fine for a team; the zone is l.diiii.xyz for now (§15 Q1).

11. The router limit, and its one-line fix

Phones ask the router; a router with rebind protection drops ponyo-k7q2.<zone> → 192.168.x.x (VERIFIED for OpenWrt default and FRITZ!Box). Installs are unaffected (they use the beacon, §8). On OpenWrt, once:

uci add_list dhcp.@dnsmasq[0].rebind_domain='l.diiii.xyz'; uci commit dhcp; /etc/init.d/dnsmasq restart

(Forum posts also show the /l.diiii.xyz/ form; unverified on dob-0 which one its dnsmasq takes — test both.) di wifi --router prints this line and the FRITZ!Box path. Offline places: the router answers itself (address=/ponyo-k7q2.l.diiii.xyz/192.168.15.53, one-local-address.md §5 b).

12. Security

  • Private key per install, made locally, never shared (atlas decision: a shared key is dangerous once a name points at a reachable address). The Cloudflare token lives only in the Worker.
  • Names only point at private or loopback addresses; a label belongs to one install key.
  • The wifi door: own names only (421), guests always, owner rights only on loopback / diiii.localhost.
  • Following needs a per-space sync key (VERIFIED: editor, one space, revocable). the wifi door hands out no keys.
  • Certificate Transparency publishes every label (VERIFIED for Tailscale, same for any public CA): <who> must be a handle, never a full name. The wildcard hides the addresses.

13. Costs

Cloudflare DNS and Workers free tier: 0 € (one door opening ≈ 3 Worker requests). Let's Encrypt: 0 €. KV free tier: 0 €. A separate domain (Q1): one yearly registration (unverified price, typically ~10–20 €). §5 B adds a DNS server on the existing VPS: 0 € but an always-on service to watch. Build: five PRs below.

14. Build plan (each one PR, about 50–85 executor tool calls)

# PR What the owner sees after
1 Name broker (Worker + tests against a fake Cloudflare API; claim, TXT, address, limits, revoke). A deploy line to run with his token; curl health. No change on installs.
2 di name: claim after di login, ACME DNS-01 through the broker, ~/.di/name/, renewal. di status: private · name ready: dob-a3f9 (certificate until …).
3 di wifi + Wifi button: runtime wifi door, guests forced, record move, QR on the panel, wiki entry; verified on a real phone. Press Wifi → phone scans → padlock, camera, WebXR.
4 Follow by name: --from <label>, beacon, last-address memory; two machines with the internet cut. di follow show --from ponyo-k7q2 works on the same wifi, offline.
5 Router help and IP changes: di wifi --router, address watcher, di status lines; (optional) §5 B DNS. A DHCP change mid-session heals itself; phones blocked by the router get the one line.

15. Questions only the owner can answer

2026-10-29 (owner): di-studio.xyz is being dropped (not renewed); the kept domains are diiii.xyz and thedi.studio. The zone is l.diiii.xyz until thedi.studio is on Cloudflare (owed: add the zone there and change its nameservers at GoDaddy; then ZONE and DI_NAME_BROKER move and names get new certificates). The broker writes only <label>.<zone> records and its token is scoped to that one zone.

  1. Zone (decided 2026-10-29, ledger N1418.10/.11): l.diiii.xyz, broker https://name.diiii.xyz; a separate domain, so a broker breach never touches thedi.studio and the certificate limit is its own. - Why not l.thedi.studio: thedi.studio is not a Cloudflare zone (its nameservers are GoDaddy's, ns67/68.domaincontrol.com), so the broker cannot write records there. - Owed move: when the owner moves thedi.studio to Cloudflare (GoDaddy → Domains → thedi.studio → Nameservers → "Change" → enter the two nameservers Cloudflare shows for the zone; Cloudflare then imports the records), the zone can become l.thedi.studio. It is a config value (ZONE in wrangler.toml, DI_NAME_ZONE on an install), so the move is one value, not code; installs already named keep their name until they re-claim. - Reviewer's note (Opus R20): diiii.xyz also carries live hosts (dev, prod, name). Mitigation: the broker writes only <label>.<zone> and _acme-challenge.<label>.<zone> records (its name guard rejects any other name), and its CF_API_TOKEN is scoped to Zone → DNS → Edit on diiii.xyz only.
  2. Label: <who>-<4 chars> from the di login handle, or fully random? Recommend the handle form — people say "follow ponyo", and CT logs see only a handle.
  3. Stateless DNS (§5 B): run our own nameserver for the address-in-name form, or stay on broker records? Recommend broker records now, nameserver only if opening the door is delayed or Cloudflare writes become a problem.
